column4: Office for Reparations Act, No. 34 of 2018
(1) The Office for Reparations may make rules for

column3: matters which rules are required to be made.

column4: (2) Every rule made under this Act shall be placed before

column3: Parliament and published in the Gazette within a reasonable
period not exceeding three months.

column4: (3) The Policies on Reparations and guidelines approved

column3: by the Cabinet of Ministers shall be placed before Parliament
and published in the Gazette within a reasonable period not
exceeding three months.

column4: (4) Notwithstanding the provisions of this Act, Policies

column3: on Reparations and guidelines authorizing disbursement of
funds  shall  be  placed  before  Parliament  for  approval  and
published  in  the  Gazette  within  a  reasonable  period  not
exceeding three months, and any disbursement in terms of
such  Policies  on  Reparations  and  guidelines  shall  only  be
effected after such approval.

column4: (1) The members of the Office for Reparations (for

column3: the limited purpose of their functions under this Act) and the
officers and servants shall be deemed to be public servants
for the purposes of the Penal Code (Chapter 19), the Bribery
Act (Chapter 26) and the Evidence Ordinance (Chapter 14).

column4: (2) The Office for Reparations shall be deemed to be a

column3: scheduled institution within the meaning of the Bribery Act
(Chapter 26), and the provisions of that Act shall be construed
accordingly.

column4: (1) The Office for Reparations may delegate to the

column3: Chief    Executive  Officer,  or  any  other  member  or  officer
thereof, any of its powers and functions.

column4: (2) The  Chief  Executive  Officer,  member  or  officer  to

column3: whom  any  of  the  powers  or  functions  of  the  Office  for
Reparations has been delegated shall exercise and perform
such powers and functions subject to the general or specific
directions of the Office for Reparations.
